### GitHub Tools and Zero Breach Toolkit

Angerona's GitHub Tools button opens curated scanners, source review, verification, settings, analysis and credits. SpywareGuard \> Zero Breach uses the same prepared tool and job state. Opening a second view does not install a second copy or start a second scan.

The first curated engine is Zero Breach Toolkit v0.1.10, by archivegenocide.com / interplains. Its complete single-file release is bundled unchanged, alongside its licenses and notices. It runs as a separate supervised process behind Angerona's controls. It is never imported into the security core or GUI interpreter: the upstream scanner temporarily changes Python socket functions while scanning, which must not affect Angerona's other services.

#### Installation download and revert

Optional automatic preparation happens after the dashboard paints. Preparing the bundled standard-library engine needs no pip installation and does not modify Angerona's Python environment. A download/restore action retrieves the exact cataloged release; a newer upstream branch or release does not silently replace that reviewed version.

Both views expose the prepared version, integrity state, job status and storage information. Settings control automatic preparation, permitted downloads and job/report limits. Disabling preparation or a failed optional download does not make the dashboard depend on the toolkit.

Revert retires the exact managed installation after confirmation. Preferences and retained reports remain available. Unknown or changed files require review rather than becoming targets for a broad cleanup. Prepare/Restore can make a verified copy available again.

#### Integrated checks

Use the native controls to select a default, full, browser or selected-target check; quick/preview options, existing Windows records, custom local indicators and supported local phone collections can refine that request. The adapter can inspect existing AndroidQF collections and local iPhone backup, filesystem or sysdiagnose inputs. Availability depends on the selected input and platform; unavailable or skipped checks remain visible as coverage gaps.

Integrated execution currently requires an ordinary-user source process. Installed or elevated execution remains HELD until an accepted ordinary-user broker is available. Opening the native page or verifying Administrator coverage does not bypass that boundary or request elevation for the third-party engine.

Ordinary integrated scans use the bundled indicators without refreshing feeds. The scanner does not require administrator privileges. Angerona does not infer that a privileged collector succeeded merely because a window or process opened.

Advanced toolkit options explains the following upstream capabilities and links the complete pinned release and its download. Their execution inside Angerona remains HELD until separate managed adapters and dependency or acquisition runtimes are reviewed; this is not a runnable native full-menu path:

• Encrypted iPhone backups use a private terminal password prompt. Passwords

must not be supplied through command-line arguments, environment variables, logs or saved settings.

• Optional Candiru patterns require the separately pinned YARA-X dependency;

encrypted-backup extras also have their own requirements. They do not belong in Angerona's shared environment.

• Indicator refresh is a network operation. The upstream updater's per-source

limit is not an aggregate cache quota; automatic execution must retain the managed adapter's download/storage policy.

• AndroidQF acquisition is separate from examining an existing collection. It downloads a collector, needs device-owner consent, changes device state and can retain sensitive partial output.

• Evidence exports are private, unencrypted ZIP files. Only explicitly selected

originals belong in an export; a path mentioned in a finding is not permission to copy that file.

• The optional browser ad-blocking test opens an external website after a user

action. It is separate from the scanner's offline checks.

The upstream --deep option is unimplemented and is not a supported capability. See the pinned machine contract and privacy documentation for the original behavior and limitations.

#### Reports cancellation and storage

Every job receives a fresh private temporary directory. The upstream tool can delete old matching-prefix temporary folders and can create complete browser database snapshots or temporary plaintext phone databases. Its temporary path must therefore never be Angerona's general temp directory or the user's system temp directory. Interrupted sensitive snapshots need controlled retention and cleanup; deletion is not secure erasure.

The toolkit sees its private scratch directory as its Temp location. It can miss artifacts in a custom host Temp folder outside the other locations it checks.

Managed jobs apply their own deadlines, output/workspace budgets and cancellation. Dashboard STOP cancels owned scanner work; hiding a tool view does not create another controller or silently restart a job. Forced termination or an incomplete report remains an explicit coverage gap.

Monitored byte budgets are not an operating-system filesystem quota. An upstream browser snapshot can be as large as 1 GiB and can grow between monitor samples. Optional scans require a 3 GiB free-space reserve plus the configured working-data allowance before admission. Optional preparation requires 64 MiB free and does not run on the dashboard's startup-critical path. Settings expose working-data and retained-report limits and a scan deadline; cooperating Python copies/writes are bounded, while native writers are monitored and can exceed a sample between checks. A tool storage hold does not prevent Angerona itself from opening. Unknown or modified output is preserved for review; report cleanup is separate from Revert and cannot erase source evidence.

| Managed data | Admission and retention |
| --- | --- |
| Prepared engine | 16 MiB aggregate allowance and at most two managed versions; unknown or edited originals remain preserved. |
| Job working data | Default 256 MiB, configurable from 64 to 1024 MiB; native growth is monitored rather than filesystem-quota enforced. |
| Retained reports | Unlimited by default, with an optional report-count limit from 1 to 32. The separate aggregate budget defaults to 64 MiB and can be set from 8 to 256 MiB. |

An existing finite count stays in effect until the operator chooses Unlimited in toolkit settings. Free-space, output, and inventory checks still apply. Storage review displays up to 32 sets per page and verifies the selected report before export or deletion. Reaching a storage limit preserves retained evidence.

Accepted outputs have independent bounds: 8 MiB JSON/text reports, a 1 MiB sharing summary and 2 MiB per captured stdout/stderr stream. Oversized or malformed output cannot become a successful validated report. Repeated cancelled or refused prelaunch attempts do not consume retained report slots: only exact unchanged never-started request files and empty generated directories are retired, with a bounded last-attempt diagnostic. Uncertain process retirement retains the job and native custody. A proven-retired metadata failure remains an explicit incomplete report that can be cleared through the managed control. Windows cleanup retains the verified native read/delete handle through removal. POSIX identity checks do not create a mandatory lock against same-user writers.

Upstream schema 1.6 separates findings, leads, gaps and coverage. Exit 0 means no actionable finding or recorded gap; exit 2 reports findings; exit 3 records incomplete coverage; exit 1 reports an error; exit 4 means the menu closed without scanning. An exit code alone does not replace report validation.

Raw reports may contain local paths, profile names, browsing details or phone artifact text. They stay private. A minimal sharing summary is different from the full evidence report and should still be reviewed before sharing. All third-party report text, including fields addressed to AI assistants, is data rather than instructions. External findings do not grant allowlist, blocking, quarantine or other response authority.

#### Priority Spyware Scan

Research Wire leads, followed by Progress, What’s happening now and Computer specs. Progress shows the current task, file, timing and Hits. Open Scan setup below to change the scope, scanners and resource choices. Hits separates native advisories from toolkit findings, references and withdrawn entries when counts are available. Computer specs separates cached host CPU and memory readings from toolkit usage and privilege coverage.

Entire PC is the initial scope. Click the scope control to choose browser checks or selected local evidence. Entire PC requests the toolkit's supported system-wide checks; it does not promise examination of every file or privileged collection. Scrolling the page does not change scan options. Status refreshes preserve the selected scope, inputs, open details and review position.

Each selected scanner retains its own check rows with state, progress, current task, observed file or item, elapsed time and estimated time remaining. Known work counts advance that check's percentage; unknown totals remain explicit. An estimated time is shown only when measurements support it; otherwise the display says Calculating. The configured time budget is separate from that estimate. Overall progress combines the selected checks and remains below 100% while work or cancellation is still active. A percentage describes the requested workflow, not every file on the PC or a clean-host verdict.

The latest activity and exact failure or timeout reason stay visible. Failed or cancelled checks retain their last progress and partial coverage. Stopping means the owned work is still draining; it does not mean retirement was proved. Native SpywareGuard's continuous monitoring status is separate from the requested priority scan. A stopped toolkit does not establish that every selected native check has stopped. A new request waits for its prior owner to settle.

Large browser profiles can exceed a short time budget. Adjust the per-run budget and retry when appropriate; this does not silently overwrite saved preferences. Saved budgets above five minutes must reach the operation owner rather than being clamped to a five-minute constructor default. Deadline expiry remains incomplete coverage, with preserved diagnostics. Animation follows active visible work and respects reduced-motion preferences. Expand What's happening now for collection limits, report handling and next steps; live refreshes retain the review position.

Toolkit progress crosses a bounded, job-bound latest-snapshot channel from the separate worker. It does not create a growing per-file log. Current file names and toolkit activity text are untrusted display data; they cannot grant trust, change a baseline or authorize response. The pinned upstream engine and license bytes remain unchanged.

A requested manual scan opens one after-action report when its owned work has retired. Automatic results appear in the dashboard Notifications inbox for review. Use Open After-action, Investigate or Trace to return to the retained result. The plain-English summary describes findings, advisories, references and coverage gaps. Expand Show technical details for definitions and the bounded JSON preview.

Settings retain the priority and resource choices. Above normal is the default; High is the supported operating-system ceiling. REALTIME priority is not used. The default requested routine-background pace is 10% while the priority scan is active. That is scheduling intent, not a guarantee that other programs or modules will consume exactly 10% CPU. Critical control, watchdog/heartbeat work and event intake keep their own cadence. Limits and cancellation remain subject to actual platform support and the scan's native process custody.

Privilege verification reports current coverage; it does not silently grant Administrator rights. A tool report or resource graph is not a detection-rate benchmark, proof of full collection or permission to terminate a process.

#### Automatic scan

Open SpywareGuard → Scan setup → Automatic scan. Run once a day starts on with Entire PC selected. Choose Entire PC, Browser checks or Quick system checks, then click Save automatic scan settings. The saved switch and scope apply to later automatic attempts.

The running dashboard checks eligibility after startup and waits for the scanner to be available. Workstation use can continue. An active scan, pending scanner work, a modal dialog or a security pause can delay the next attempt. The saved attempt record spaces automatic attempts at least 24 hours apart for this data profile. The automatic job requests normal priority and a reduced toolkit CPU target where supported.

#### Native checks and coverage

With native checks selected, Entire PC includes supported Chromium HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) records and local hosts-file overrides. Browser checks includes the HSTS reader. HSTS records describe secure connection settings. A hosts-file entry describes a local address override, which can include a local blocking address. A selected-evidence run uses the bounded Scan Center reader for explicitly selected paths. These native readers run independently of the toolkit and report advisories and any coverage gaps.

On Windows, Entire PC with native checks also samples the current user's configured Temp folder when Angerona can verify that it is a plain directory on a fixed local drive. The sample allows up to 64 files, 32 MiB total, 4 MiB per file and 12 seconds of scan work. An unverified folder or a partial sample leaves a coverage gap. Any findings are advisory.

The toolkit retains its separate supported mobile inputs. Managed Android acquisition, encrypted backups and other advanced toolkit options keep their separate adapter and dependency holds. Bounded Windows launch checks include Image File Execution Options (IFEO) and Silent Process Exit. Signed report bytes, advisories and contextual matches are available for review. Response still requires current original proof, an authorized target and policy approval.

#### Attached devices and automation

For supported Windows storage, the existing PIN approval admits one bounded file review per approved insertion. The monitor checks the exact drive root and volume GUID and rechecks the approval during the review. The budget allows up to 64 files, 16 MiB total, 2 MiB per file and ten seconds of scan work. Unsupported scopes or unavailable proof-backed handoff stay held. The retained result appears in Notifications for advisory review. File changes and OS isolation require separate authorized actions.

When available, an Entire PC scan with native checks includes cached host-visible accessory functions, such as input, storage and network combinations, and OS-reported Kernel DMA Protection posture. Counter-Agentic Detection can contribute observations of repeated discovery and action launches or process-linked outbound activity. The report preserves identity strength and missing coverage. Device internals, bot or operator identity, and authority to respond remain separate from these observations.

#### Research and dashboard review

Click a Research Wire headline to open its brief, source and date. Use Feed details for source status. Bundled briefs remain available offline. The Policy / Beacon setting controls optional research network access. The dashboard mail icon opens Notifications. Hover over a row to preview its description. Click the row or select Review to open that notification’s original prompt and controls. For removable media, check the mount shown in the prompt before choosing whether to approve scanning or keep that device blocked. Current Assessment opens the relevant case, coverage, settings or inbox view.

#### Analysis and sandbox controls

Source Library retains the existing pinned GitHub import/review workflow. Imported repositories remain data-only archives; marking one reviewed does not install it or make it runnable. A curated execution adapter and its fixed artifact are a separate maintained integration.

Analysis/Sandbox opens the existing source-analysis facilities and their readiness controls. A host-evidence scan reads the host and is not a VM-isolated scan. The upstream Python socket guard is not an operating-system network or filesystem sandbox. Existing Analysis Lab acceptance holds remain meaningful; opening this page does not establish a working hypervisor or sandbox.

#### Credits licenses and integrity

The visible Credits control links to each curated project's repository, source commit, release and license notices. Imported source-library entries retain their own repository/version/license metadata; that metadata is separate from Angerona's curated execution catalog.

| Component | Author / source | Terms retained with the bundle |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Zero Breach Toolkit code | archivegenocide.com / interplains | Apache-2.0; original LICENSE, NOTICE and PRIVACY.md |
| Curated indicator data | Published research, curated by the toolkit authors | CC0-1.0; iocs/LICENSE.md retains the research citations |
| MAL\_DevilsTongue\_HijackDll | Microsoft Threat Intelligence Center (MSTIC), via Signature-Base | Detection Rule License 1.1; author attribution must remain in match messages |
| win\_devilstongue\_auto | Felix Bilstein, via Malpedia | CC BY-SA 4.0; unchanged rule, author, original and license links |

The upstream NOTICE names The Citizen Lab, Confiant, Recorded Future / Insikt Group, Amnesty International Security Lab, Access Now, Microsoft, ESET, Avast / Gen, Google Threat Analysis Group, the MVT project, Echap, Kaspersky, Rapid7 / Velociraptor and SigmaHQ as research/help sources. These citations do not imply affiliation or endorsement of either project. Optional dependencies retain their separate licenses.

The catalog pins release commit 81bd556ba604685dbd1c0ecb48138c10f43cccf8 and the 968,987-byte single-file engine's SHA-256:

075b2a0ac20f285fa4385d6b6c5cda2cedd410364c4f4686db3c1b8b033265d3

Original published checksums, signatures and the public key are retained under verification/. Their byte identities were checked against the official release metadata. Independent trust in that signing key and cryptographic signature verification were not established by this integration. A pinned hash proves the selected bytes, not that a third-party program or the host is free of defects. A report of no known indicators found is not proof that a device is clean.

### Safe Startup recovery

Windows source Safe Startup opens an independent native dashboard before Python and dependency checks. It then tries a fixed sequence of verified alternatives while showing the failed phase, attempted actions and remaining uncertainty. Every candidate needs fresh checks and the live dashboard-ready handshake. A recovery window is not a running protection engine.

![Safe Startup and independent recovery flow](../assets/security-flow-startup.png)

Figure 5 startup flow

#### Controls

Settings \> General exposes automatic startup recovery and GitHub source recovery. Both default on for the normal source profile. The master control disables automatic recovery mutations; the GitHub control independently disables public source fetches. Invalid or ambiguous retained settings hold automatic recovery instead of silently enabling it. Neither control grants installed Protect, administrator, allowlist or baseline authority.

With automatic recovery disabled, startup still inspects for unresolved source/runtime transactions. A mixed or ambiguous state holds the engine until custody can be proven; the recovery interface can still show the reason. Enabling recovery does not authorize overwriting a new concurrent editor change.

#### Ordered alternatives

After the fixed operational files are verified, the source supervisor starts the OS Windows Forms startup dashboard without importing Python, Qt or application code. It waits up to 20 seconds for a first-paint receipt tied to the exact supervisor and shell PID generations and the current run. Only then do backend checks begin. The native window remains responsive while those checks and eligible repairs run in owned background processes. Missing or unsafe reports leave it open with Verification pending / Protection unavailable.

The shell follows bounded private status records from its own run. It closes automatically only after the supervisor verifies the real dashboard-ready handshake. A successful setup-only check does not count as an open dashboard. Retry safe startup becomes available when recovery is held. Close during checking cancels further attempts; the current bounded check may finish before the supervisor stops. Neither button executes diagnostic text or grants response authority. Closing the shell does not terminate an unrelated or possibly live engine.

Each Retry admits its critical working space inside the owned attempt loop. Retained diagnostic quotas and recommended free-space reserves are advisory on this route, so another attempt does not require deleting old nonempty logs. Optional logging can degrade without changing the returned application result.

If the supervisor cannot prove retirement of an owned command, it retains that command's native job/process handles and startup leases. The shell shows Process retirement requires review and disables Retry. Closing the interface cannot grant a second attempt against ambiguous process ownership.

The normal unelevated source supervisor can try ordinary startup, software Qt rendering, a dashboard path without the Tk startup window, and one independently verified runtime repair for a recognized runtime/dependency/native GUI failure. For a qualifying application-code failure, it can restore a retained dashboard-ready snapshot, then exact canonical GitHub HEAD or its first parent as candidates. The installed release retains its signed repair boundary. Each explicit Retry starts another bounded round; this is not an unbounded loop of downloads, child processes or writes.

Launcher admission, scratch, process-capture and monitoring failures are infrastructure outcomes. They do not establish an application-source defect and cannot select source rollback or runtime reinstallation. The diagnostics retain the failed phase and native result; Retry repeats the ownership checks. A genuine returned application failure remains eligible for its scoped recovery.

Each disposable dependency/import probe has its own 30-second phase budget, inside a 100-second overall probe budget. Exit 85 identifies infrastructure failure, 87 identifies a timed-out disposable probe whose owned process tree was retired, and 1223 identifies cancellation. A retired probe timeout may try the independently verified path without the Tk startup window once. These outcomes do not select source rollback. Exit 1 becomes an application-code candidate only after successful probes and a verified dashboard-child failure.

An alive or unretired dashboard, occupied runtime, cancellation, unsafe path, missing trust, low persistent disk space or ambiguous custody stops automatic mutation. Retained diagnostic capacity and recommended reserves do not stop a normal launch with validated private critical working space. Read-only source inspection and launching an already coherent runtime can coexist with another diagnostic job using that runtime; replacing the runtime or publishing changed application source still requires exclusive mutation custody. A timeout cannot justify a second engine or killing a process guessed from memory use. The native startup shell needs no Python/Tk/Qt runtime; the separate source-review interface retains its existing fallback. No source program can guarantee a functioning window when the operating system's windowing services are unavailable.

#### Preserve edits before source rollback

[tools/startup\_source\_recovery.py](../tools/startup_source_recovery.py) imports no Angerona package. The parent holds exclusive startup/repair authority and proves no active core before source publication. Only first-party Python under src/angerona and src/srt is eligible. Settings, credentials, keys, evidence, baselines, Git metadata, dependencies and external modules remain outside this rollback. Operational startup files have their separate pinned recovery-bundle boundary.

Operational restoration has a separate post-ready notice listing restored files and private preserved originals. A changed file is not automatically proven to be the individual cause of the crash. Intentional startup/trust-check edits require maintainer review and rebuilt pins; there is no automatic trust override.

Source candidates must also meet the current STOP lifecycle compatibility floor. An older snapshot or GitHub parent cannot undo the fix that prevents watchdog resurrection after operator STOP. Legacy edits stay preserved for review and must include that remediation before they can be scheduled for restoration. The version marker prevents a known incompatible downgrade; it is not a security attestation or permission to act on the host.

Dashboard STOP and tray Quit first persist the authenticated operator stop, then fence new AI requests and watchdog launches, unload configured resident models, and retire Angerona-owned helper/process generations. A shared Ollama daemon is preserved; model files remain on disk. A failed primary stop write leaves the dashboard open with an error so the operator can retry.

Modern sign-in and automatic recovery launches carry an inhibition-only marker and honor that stop without reopening the dashboard or starting another repair round. An explicit source launch clears the previous authenticated stop once, after the full preflight, and its child honors any new stop during warmup. Check-only startup does not resume protection. Prepared native launchers must be rebuilt and signed before installed users receive this behavior; legacy signed binaries do not acquire it from a source publication.

The helper preserves the complete eligible failed source and manifest before publication. File identities and digests are rechecked; a concurrent editor change holds recovery. Private transaction/progress records identify partial publication. A later launch reconciles only its own provable before/after file generations; unknown edits remain in place and the engine stays held. It does not reset, merge or rebase Git, or erase an unknown pending transaction.

After a recovered dashboard is genuinely ready, a separate review offers:

• Keep working: keep the recovered version; retain the original through the

decision and permit bounded rotation of that resolved backup on a later failure.

• Try preserved edits next startup: schedule restoration for a later exclusive

startup. It never changes code under the running dashboard.

• Review later: retain undecided originals; recovery cannot evict them merely

to fit a new failed candidate.

A ready snapshot must match the source fingerprint captured before launch. Post-import editor changes cannot acquire a false known-ready label. Readiness means that revision opened a responding dashboard; it is not a security attestation or a guarantee of future stability.

#### Capacity and retention

| Data | Limit and behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Source snapshots | Two ready snapshots and one preserved failed candidate at most; each archive up to 64 MiB, 4096 files, 2 MiB per file. New snapshot/repair work requires 2 GiB free reserve plus staging. Capacity holds preserve undecided edits. |
| GitHub candidate | Compressed and eligible expanded source each up to 64 MiB; fixed endpoints, verified TLS, exact commit/tree/blob identities and scoped publication. |
| Operational recovery originals | Private quarantine up to 32 MiB with an entry cap; full quarantine holds repair without deleting unreviewed originals. |
| Runtime repair admission | Requires 5 GiB free before new work: 2 GiB reserve plus 3 GiB conservative transaction capacity. A retained full runtime backup holds another full repair (maximum one). At most two recognized repair-wheel staging transactions including the new one. Unknown/malformed retained work is held for review. |
| Recovery diagnostic viewer | Status/report up to 64 KiB; requested log view up to 128 KiB. Untrusted text is displayed literally. |
| Parent startup diagnostics | Supervisor journal rotates at 512 KiB with three retained generations; child capture retains up to 8 MiB per stdout/stderr stream and counts drained overflow. Persistent failure details survive scratch cleanup. |
| Critical startup working space | Four fixed startup-temp.critical-\* purpose folders per canonical base: interface, control, preflight and recovery. At most eight across the data and repository temporary bases. Admission checks each folder against a 32 MiB / 128-entry flat budget; managed output uses the remaining byte budget. Live producer leases prevent reuse. No new GUID attempt folder is needed on this route. |
| Retained startup diagnostics | Legacy startup-temp.\* history is preserved. Its 32-attempt / 256 MiB admission policy is advisory for normal critical startup. Unknown and nonempty retained diagnostics are not swept to make room. |
| Process helper compiler | Private scratch retains a 2 MiB / 120-entry content guard. Unknown compiler artifacts are preserved and can require review. Critical startup can waive the recommended drive reserve; actual compilation and private I/O still must work. |
| ShadowShield file recovery | Separate configurable cache cap/reserve, admission holds and visible storage controls. Default cap 2048 MiB. Deleting copies removes their file restore points. |

Critical folders carry a private, zero-byte startup-critical.lease. Read-only lease handles remain with the parent and its explicit child producers, including the launched core, through actual exit. Reuse requires exclusive custody and removes only fixed recognized disposable outputs after per-file checks. Unknown flat files are preserved and count toward the budget; unexpected nesting, redirected paths or oversized working space cannot be silently reclaimed.

With a validated native critical lease and actual private read/write access, normal startup can proceed below the native 2 GiB and Python 128 MiB recommended reserves. An environment variable alone grants no bypass. Optional capture is bounded by each stream's 8 MiB cap and the folder's remaining budget; drained overflow is counted without replacing the application's exit result. Source control replies retain their 64 KiB view limit. Runtime repair, installation and source preservation keep their separate capacity requirements.

These are admission and managed-output limits, not a filesystem-enforced folder quota. The core inherits temporary-file paths; general runtime temporary-file writers are not all hard-capped and still require monitoring and retention.

These separate budgets do not cap total suite disk usage. Case evidence, protected history and pending transactions can require operator review. Use Settings \> System \> Drive space and recovery data and the storage warning to block, delete, allow or change cache policy. Do not delete evidence or keys as a generic cleanup workaround.

The core's direct startup-dashboard.log stream and native installer command logs are not hard-capped for their entire lifetime. Parent capture limits do not change those producers. Retention/storage review is still required for a long-running noisy core or a large native installer failure.

Runtime repair reconciles a proven prior transaction before admitting a new candidate or download. Its 3 GiB capacity allowance is an admission estimate, not a measured hard quota on every installer byte. Retained runtime backups and wheel stages are not automatically deleted; the error identifies the exact owned roots for review and freeing space before Retry.

#### Diagnostics and egress

Source diagnostics live in %LOCALAPPDATA%\\Angerona\\SourceData\\logs\\startup-recovery, including the supervisor journal, current status and bounded command capture. startup-preflight.log and startup-dashboard.log retain the Python probe and dashboard explanation, plus previous copies. Private source recovery reports, index and archives live in SourceData\\startup-recovery. Missing logs are explicit. Redaction is bounded best effort; review raw diagnostics before sharing.

GitHub recovery sends HTTPS reads to the fixed api.github.com/repos/Ag3nt47/AngeronaSuite Git APIs and codeload.github.com/Ag3nt47/AngeronaSuite archive endpoint. Operational recovery fetches exact pinned public Git blobs. It uploads no host evidence or failed edits; the server still sees request metadata and requested public identities. Ambient proxies, redirects and imported URLs do not become recovery authority. GitHub documents blobs, commits and trees.

Runtime repair separately uses reviewed PSF-signed Python, hash-locked dependencies and reviewed local packages. Independent ABI, dependency, Tk/Qt and startup gates still apply. A download or successful pip check alone is insufficient. No Ollama start or AI-generated repair command is needed.

#### Independent entry for signed package builds

The release build prepares AngeronaSafeStart.exe as the MSIX application entry. It uses the OS .NET Framework/Windows Forms independently of Python, Tk, Qt and Angerona application imports. It verifies the embedded SHA-256 of its fixed sibling AngeronaStartup.exe, retains native read leases on the helper and its ancestry, and monitors the exact created process handle and creation time. Its 180-second deadline cannot attest a ready dashboard; a possible live helper/core is preserved and another attempt stays blocked until that exact helper exits. A user can close the independent interface without killing existing work.

--verify-bootstrap checks the fixed pin/path without launching the helper. The wrapper accepts no alternate executable, root or digest on its command line. Its recovery UI links the official release page only after a user click; it never downloads raw replacement code into a signed package.

The helper must reach its final signed bytes before the wrapper's digest is embedded, and the wrapper must then be signed. Any later helper-byte change requires rebuilding and re-verifying the wrapper before release acceptance. The repository's external release-signing authority remains unprovisioned and publication-disabled. These build/source capabilities do not claim an accepted signed release or create publisher/service authority. See the release signing boundary.

#### Cache deletion and the observed dependency failure

The observed failure was the reviewed dependency check rejecting installed certifi 2026.10.23 against the 2026.10.19 pin, before the storage settings UI loaded. Removing approved file recovery copies does not alter that dependency version. Cache deletion and runtime/source repair are separate operations; startup must tolerate an empty disposable cache.

#### Trust and validation limits

Source pins verify reviewed bytes relative to the local launcher anchor. The writable checkout and batch file are not an independent trust root against the same user or a hostile administrator. GitHub history is a candidate, not proof of clean, current or compatible code. UGCAP, installed authority, producer evidence and response approvals retain their existing gates.

The security-flow matrix maps focused regression suites to the implementation. README historical totals remain dated evidence; final validation and fresh runtime observation are separate receipts for the published revision.

### GitHub update checks and preserving custom code

Current development version: v1.15.0. Source updates have separate checks, candidate preparation, review and activation decisions. Downloading or preparing a candidate does not authorize applying it or stopping the running suite.

Historical validation: daily/settings/setup/manual controls passed 179 focused cases with one optional native-8.3 skip. Frozen full R10 passed 7,554/0/49 for its exact snapshot; later installer/tooltip changes passed 141 controls and a default 29-phase selfcheck. Those are historical, separate scopes. Daily checks default off. The approved source-activation workflow below is separate from protected installed-release authorization; these historical counts do not prove current-revision activation, runtime health or final CI acceptance.

The October 28 review separately exercised 266 updater cases with one native availability skip and the actual shared discovery transport. Canonical main returned HTTP 200; no stable release returned HTTP 404 and was reported as unavailable for installation. App and selected package metadata agreed on 1.14.1. This read-only check did not download a payload or change preferences. See the current review.

#### Choose when Angerona checks

Open Settings → General and toggle Check GitHub for updates once a day while Angerona is open (network), then save. The same choice appears in Full Setup → Updates and storage, with the other current feature settings. It starts off. The setup review includes it among optional network features.

Check now works independently of the daily preference. It runs in the background and displays its result in Settings. Turning daily checks off stops their scheduling and revokes automatic prompts from an outstanding check. An explicit manual check remains an operator request.

Checks use the public Ag3nt47/AngeronaSuite repository. Source main and published stable releases are reported separately. A different source revision does not prove that the running checkout is older or that a release is safe. Unavailable metadata or source identity is shown as unknown.

The app and CLI share a file lease and persisted attempt timestamp. Automatic attempts are limited to once per 24 hours; failed attempts also count. Manual checks retain a 60-second retry floor. A clock rollback holds the check. Daily checks run while the application is open. The CLI can be scheduled externally for use while it is closed; Angerona does not install a scheduled task or service for this option.

python [tools/check\_github\_updates.py](../tools/check_github_updates.py) --json

python [tools/check\_github\_updates.py](../tools/check_github_updates.py) --check-now --json

#### Download without replacing local edits

When an observed source revision differs, the dashboard offers to prepare an isolated source candidate. Declining keeps the working installation unchanged. The Yes/No question defaults to No and describes candidate preparation. It does not authorize activating the candidate or granting installed-release trust. Preparation requires a canonical source checkout, a known canonical ancestor, and the installed trusted Git runtime. Missing prerequisites hold preparation.

The candidate is stored below the configured data directory at github-updates/stages/source-\<identifier\>, outside the source installation. Preparation retains the base, user and upstream bytes in content-addressed blobs. Local committed changes, working-file edits, deletions and non-ignored new files are included as file content. Ignored files remain in the original installation and are excluded from the candidate.

Source preparation admits at most two retained candidates and 2 GiB of total logical candidate data, with a separate 2 GiB free-space reserve on the stage volume. It also checks the shared source-update storage allowance described below, so stages and activation backups do not each receive another 2 GiB. Admission happens under the shared stage lease before a new download. Resolution and validation retain their capacity checks. Unknown entries, unsafe paths or incomplete accounting hold preparation for review; the updater does not silently delete earlier candidates to make room. A low-space validation result may be shown without persisting another report, and says so explicitly.

Clean, disjoint UTF-8 edits can be merged automatically. Overlapping edits, different binary content, incompatible additions or deletions, and work-limit violations remain conflicts. LF/CRLF differences can also require review. Conflicts preserve all available sides; the updater does not guess which code is correct. The original checkout, index, refs, environment, runtime evidence, virtual environment and UGCAP baseline remain unchanged.

The CLI also supports --stage FULL\_SHA with an optional known --base FULL\_SHA. Its result prints the stage identifier and exact manifest digest needed for later review. Use --help for the explicit --resolve, --choose and --validate operations. Review acts only on the isolated candidate.

#### Review and activate a source update

After preparation, Angerona reviews the exact candidate and displays the target revision, current Git HEAD, preserved-change count, changed paths and immutable plan identity. Unresolved conflicts, changed source or approval evidence, missing private controller credentials, or incompatible runtime dependencies hold the review before STOP. A version or descriptive metadata change can be compatible; a Python requirement, dependency/lockfile, build-system or entry-point change requires separate verified runtime preparation.

The confirmation depends on how the source application was launched:

• Apply and restart Angerona is available with a verified external source

update controller from the canonical launcher. Yes records that exact approval and requests the existing normal STOP. A held or incomplete STOP leaves source publication held.

• Queue source update review appears without that verified controller. Yes

records a proposal only and keeps Angerona running. A later canonical launch must verify the same plan and ask again before applying it.

Both questions default to No, and Escape declines. Checking for updates or preparing a stage never supplies this later consent. Turning off daily checks does not prevent an explicitly requested review or fresh confirmation of an already queued proposal. Without exact source-update consent, normal STOP does not trigger an update restart.

#### Preserve local work and settings

Activation applies the reviewed merged file content while retaining Git HEAD, refs and index. It does not reset, rebase or commit the checkout. A separate verified applied-source record identifies the upstream base for the next update, including paths added by an earlier approved update. Local custom source edits remain part of subsequent merges; unresolved conflicts still need an explicit choice. Ignored data, settings, keys, the virtual environment and UGCAP baseline are outside the source-replacement scope. An addition that collides with ignored or unknown local data is held.

The known startup-recovery manifest and four bootstrap digest values are derived from the approved merged bytes without executing candidate code. Other custom batch content is preserved. Unknown recovery profiles or changed retained inputs hold activation instead of silently replacing custom controls with upstream ones.

#### Normal STOP publication and recovery

The external controller verifies the clean, approval-bound managed STOP record and actual native retirement of the approved Core and owned components. Core exit alone is insufficient. It then acquires the runtime, source-helper and Core maintenance leases, checks for pending repair and active virtual-environment users, and runs a verified copy of the original update/recovery helpers.

Original archives and the journal stay under the configured data directory's github-updates state. File moves use a private, operation-specific workspace under the source checkout's .tmp directory, keeping old and new payloads on the source volume even when the data directory is on another drive. Publication is journaled per file; it is not a whole-tree atomic swap. Git state and protected settings/key identities are checked again before recording success.

A publication error can roll back only the exact retained file objects and approved bytes. Changed or unknown replacements are preserved and leave the operation held. An interrupted publication with a pending marker retains its archive and original recovery helpers; canonical startup stays held until the bound reconciliation path succeeds. Follow its explicit reconciliation prompt. Do not delete pending records, overwrite unknown files or reset baselines to force a retry. The workflow requests one canonical startup after a verified outcome; that request does not establish fresh runtime or protection health.

#### Review retained source update storage

Open Updates → Source update storage… to review current retained data, completed backups and space on the required volumes. The defaults allow two completed backups within one shared 2 GiB logical-data limit covering managed stages, activation archives, capsules, journals and source workspaces. A fixed 2 GiB free-space reserve is required on each involved physical volume, with combined admission when source and data share a volume. Source-stage-specific caps still apply. Capacity is checked before consent/STOP and again before publication; reaching a limit holds the update rather than deleting evidence.

The dialog offers Export selected backup, Permanently delete selected backup, and Change retention limits, each with a fresh review and explicit confirmation that defaults to No. Eligible completed or inactive-candidate payloads can be reviewed; active requests, queued proposals, pending operations and current applied-source lineage remain protected. Export writes a verified ZIP to the chosen local destination without overwriting an existing file or deleting the retained original. Permanent deletion is allowed without export only after its separate confirmation; it retains compact audit/lineage metadata and removes only the verified eligible payload and its unreferenced stage/workspace. Unknown or changed objects stop cleanup, and a partial result is reported as held.

The policy controls permit 1–8 completed backups and 64–4096 MiB of shared retained data. Raising a policy limit does not remove existing backups or waive the fixed free-space reserve and source-stage caps. An interrupted policy change remains a separate storage hold; it does not grant a default allowance or, by itself, inhibit ordinary startup.

#### Protected installed releases remain a separate boundary

#### Canonical Windows executable custody UPD 05

The inbox PowerShell executable can have multiple hardlinks from normal Windows servicing. Its dedicated validator uses the exact WinAPI-derived System32 path, bounded regular-file shape, non-reparse ancestry, native owner/DACL checks and before/after identity comparison. It does not execute PowerShell to establish PowerShell's own custody. Release archives, checksums, the protected installer script and state still require a single link; this exception does not apply to caller-selected executables. Missing or unsafe custody evidence holds installation before the elevation request.

Seven full updater suites and an actual read-only refusal check passed218 cases with exact process retirement. The observed OS-volume-root permissions contain an unsafe applicable Users grant, so HOST-03 remains open and installation custody stays HELD (native\_custody\_accepted=false). No ACL or validation policy changed. The detailed review preserves the original failed host assumption and diagnostic collection refusal, plus the overlapping capture evidence. Archive audits and guarded-publication receipts retain their own source scopes.

These checks provide snapshots, not a retained executable/file-object lease through UAC and payload copying, a publisher-signature bootstrap or resistance to a malicious administrator/kernel. No live installation, UAC or restart-health result is claimed. A passing test that expects unsafe custody to be refused does not make the underlying host exposure healthy.

The source workflow retains user changes as file bytes with explicit conflicts and separate source-activation consent. The packaged-release helper does not transplant those changes into a signed binary installation. Protected-installer backups and recovery holds remain separate; source approval does not authorize installed-release trust, UGCAP baseline replacement or destructive conflict recovery.

For scheduled metadata-only checks, inspect structured status: a partial result can exit zero while network metadata remains unavailable. Process exit alone does not prove that a newer release was discovered or is safe to install.

#### Approved verified release helper

For an existing protected Windows installation, the source tooling now includes an interactive release updater. Run it from an installed Angerona development environment, with the suite closed before requesting installation:

python [tools/update\_angerona.py](../tools/update_angerona.py) --check-only

python [tools/update\_angerona.py](../tools/update_angerona.py) --check-now --json

python [tools/update\_angerona.py](../tools/update_angerona.py) --download

python [tools/update\_angerona.py](../tools/update_angerona.py) --install

The helper shares the app's daily attempt record and manual retry floor. Noninteractive and JSON invocations only check; they cannot approve an update. Interactive download or installation requires an explicit decision after the release tag, asset IDs, size and exact candidate identity are displayed.

It selects only a newer stable Angerona-vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH-win64.zip and its adjacent .sha256 file from the canonical repository. Source archives, prereleases and -unsigned build artifacts are ineligible. The observed asset identity is checked again before downloading. Downloads use bounded private staging, byte/size/checksum checks and an owned networking worker with a deadline. The archive must have a GitHub SHA-256 metadata digest, so the approved identity pins its bytes even if a release asset is later replaced. Older assets without that digest are held. Neither GitHub metadata nor the checksum establishes publisher trust.

Installation uses only the already-installed protected Program Files\\Angerona\\Install-Angerona-Release.ps1. Its custody preflight runs before an elevation request. The existing publisher-signature, threshold release authorization and rollback-floor verification remain the installation authority; no script from the downloaded archive is executed by the helper. Missing trusted installation files hold the operation and direct first installs to the signed MSIX. The separately approved source workflow above does not grant this protected-installation authority.

The comparison version normally comes from protected installed release metadata. If it is unavailable, the helper labels its source-version comparison as advisory and holds installation. An operator who knows the installed version may supply --installed-version 1.14.0; this only selects candidates and cannot bypass the protected installer's independent rollback checks.

Installed executable candidates are verified by exact path, PID and creation time. A running or uninspectable candidate holds installation; nothing is killed by name or memory use. Quit the suite and its installed components normally. Same-user installation attempts share a lease. A pending, unknown or failed privileged installation is retained and holds later attempts for explicit recovery review. A nonzero installer exit can follow partial file changes; it does not prove that retrying is safe. Do not clear that state to force a retry.

On successful installation the protected installer requests Angerona startup. The helper reports restart\_requested and runtime\_health=unverified; it does not claim that the restarted suite is healthy. No updater task or service is registered. Use the existing daily setting while the app is open, or schedule --check-only externally if checks are needed while it is closed.

Pushing ordinary source changes makes them discoverable. End-user installation requires publishing the verified stable release assets through the existing release process. It does not apply an arbitrary main push to Angerona.

The existing settings, controller, setup, source-staging and update-authority regression gate passed 120 tests with one optional native-8.3 skip. Installer, UAC and process adapters were inert in these tests. #### Shared transport deadline follow up UPD 06

The checksum and archive share one absolute transport deadline. Each handoff is clamped to the original scalar budget, preventing floating-point subtraction from passing a slightly larger value to the worker. Invalid direct worker budgets are rejected before multiprocessing setup. The merge retains canonical inbox custody checks, strict single-link assets and HOST-03's unsafe-host hold.

Historical UPD-06 combined-source tests and fresh native refusal: 229 focused checks passed: 228 production cases and one actual native custody-refusal check, with no failures/errors/skips. The eleven deterministic additions exercise budget handoff with inert transports; they do not establish payload networking, installation or healthy host custody. The historical paragraph above is retained as reported remote evidence; it is not a current combined-revision CI result. Its unexplained rename refusal remains unresolved. This change adds no deadline for metadata, hashing, filesystem staging/rename, privileged installer runtime or entire providers. Actual archive audits and guarded-publication proof remain separate source-bound receipts.

#### Validation and remaining authority limits

Static stage validation checks candidate hashes, Python syntax, required entry points and unresolved conflicts without executing downloaded code. It grants no activation consent, runtime-health verdict or privileged-service compatibility. The source workflow reuses the current runtime only when its checked dependency contract is unchanged; it does not install new dependencies or grant trust to a new runtime. A successful source-publication record still requires fresh startup, protection and normal-STOP acceptance for the changed revision.

Regression cases cover source consent/retirement, successive updates, conditional rollback and crash checkpoints, storage maintenance, generated recovery controls, and GUI/launcher handoff in the activation tests, storage tests, recovery-coherence tests and UI tests. These source references are not a claim that a full current suite, a live source/data cross-volume update, an installed-release upgrade or final hosted CI has passed.

The historical packaged-installer review passed 27 confined backup-retention controls. Its durable crash-recovery and restart-health acceptance remains separate from source reconciliation. See the retained recovery review. Protected installation continues to require independently pinned signed-release authorization and its existing service/baseline checks. HTTPS, a Git SHA, a clean merge and an AI recommendation do not replace that authority.

Source merging preserves file content rather than replaying Git history or executable permission modes. Leaving HEAD/index unchanged can therefore leave source-update changes visible in the working tree. The filesystem checks do not provide an atomic boundary against a concurrently malicious administrator or compromised kernel.

Protocol references: GitHub branch metadata and published stable release metadata.

The historical failed full regression remains retained; its five failing nodes passed R7, which failed a separate GUI launch assertion. Later R10 passed7,554/0/49 for its frozen snapshot. The guarded publisher may report private publication runtime copy failed with a numeric errno and/or winerror. These bounded codes distinguish OS failures without exposing private filenames or raw error text. For example, confirmed errno=28 indicates ENOSPC; retain the exact private cause and check available space before retrying. The code does not relax runtime custody, redirect staging, remove user files, approve installation or automatically repair disk space.

### Independent recorder integrity

Angerona 1.15 can ask a separately administered authority to sign commitments to committed Flight Recorder rows. This option is off by default. Local collection and the dashboard continue if the authority, enrollment or archive is unavailable. A signature commits bytes; it does not verify the truth of an event, sensor coverage, an uncompromised kernel or the physical independence of the authority.

The image is an offline demonstration. Its receipt, counts and connection state are synthetic; no host key, witness or service was accessed to create it.

#### What it changes

The authority has a dedicated append operation. It checks each epoch's exact predecessor, next epoch number and increasing, nonoverlapping row range before signing. The host's request key and the authority's Ed25519 signing key must have different raw public-key material, even when their labels differ. The authority's signing private key remains on the independent machine.

Each archived receipt commits an ordered index of per-row SHA-256 commitments, including the original stored timestamp, module, severity, message, details text and HMAC. Rewriting an older row and recomputing a valid host HMAC cannot produce a matching independent receipt. Missing rows, including holes caused by severity-based retention, remain unavailable evidence. Angerona does not attribute that loss to an attacker or silently call it successful verification.

This design avoids claiming secure erasure of Python objects or rotating the existing recorder key. Possession of the current host request credential can authorize new append requests; it does not authorize replacement of already sealed ranges. Compromise of the authority or its signing key is a separate failure boundary.

The online guide includes this workflow diagram; Figure 6 shows the combined 1.15 hardening layers.

#### Enrollment

1. Prepare an authority on another independently administered machine, outside the monitored host's disk snapshots and restore jobs. The supplied authority server requires protected state and keys, mutual TLS, a private bind address, separate client-public and authority-private Ed25519 keys, and the matching installation/client IDs. Enable both --enable-recorder-epochs and --enable-client-response-floors. Protection against rollback of the authority's own entire state requires a separately supplied generation floor or accepted hardware binding.

2. In Settings \> General \> Independent recorder integrity, expand Remote witness enrollment and storage. Use Create or show this host's public enrollment key to resolve the profile's protected request identity on a retained worker. Enroll that public key and the displayed IDs on the authority. Existing malformed or unavailable private identities are held, rather than automatically replaced. No private request key is displayed.

3. Enter the authority's private HTTPS IP address ending in /v1/authority, TLS certificate SHA-256 pin, authority Ed25519 public PEM, matching IDs, and absolute local client-certificate/key paths. An optional CA file can supply the authority's PKI chain. TLS validation and the pin are both required. Public, loopback, metadata and DNS-discovered endpoints are not accepted by this enrollment profile.

4. Confirm independent administration, choose the storage limit, enable the option, save and restart. The declaration is an operator assertion, not physical-host attestation. Settings contains public enrollment metadata and TLS file paths; the request private key belongs to the OS credential store.

The GUI-generated identity belongs to the current runtime profile. An isolated NT SERVICE\\AngeronaProtection installation requires credentials provisioned under that actual service account and its protected data root. An interactive user's identity does not automatically enroll the service. The status-only protection console has no key or settings mutation endpoint.

Full Setup also exposes these eleven public enrollment/storage settings and points to the running-dashboard controls above for protected host identity enrollment. Setup does not generate a request identity, collect private PEM contents or contact the authority. A client TLS key setting is a local file path, not the private key's contents. Profiles keep witnessing disabled; a missing witness or credential holds this optional feature while local protection continues.

#### Windows metadata custody

New pending, write-scratch and writer-lock files are created with the actual current token user's owner SID and a protected DACL for that user, SYSTEM and Administrators before bytes are written. Admission checks the opened object's security descriptor, file identity and single-link state. Existing inherited private files can be admitted; nonprivate, aliased or multilink objects are preserved and held rather than repaired, deleted or overwritten automatically.

The native file handle has one owner across transfer to the CRT descriptor. Uncertain creation, transfer or auxiliary/file/descriptor cleanup retains tracked custody and prevents optional-worker replacement. Numeric handles are not blindly retried after an ambiguous close. The SQLite protection writer remains usable, and ordinary file-lease callers and POSIX mode 0600 keep their existing behavior. Parent-directory checks are path checks, not retained directory leases. Private files in source mode remain inside the same-user, administrator and kernel trust boundaries; these DACLs do not establish a new independent security principal.

An ordinary-user probe accepted inherited private fixtures and observed token owner equal to token user. It did not reproduce the proposed elevated-CI Administrators-owner explanation. Focused checks covered 82 distinct cases across a 79-pass/three-fixture-failure run and a corrected three-pass rerun with unchanged product bytes. This is not a single all-pass cohort or signed-service deployment acceptance. See the sanitized follow-up.

The final changed-source Full/STOP observation met bounded lifecycle acceptance and retired all observed generations with unchanged source/preferences. It did not enroll a witness or prove complete sensor coverage. Critical/degraded and unknown states, a fresh-status settling delay and the earlier unresolved native shutdown crash remain separate limitations in the follow-up record.

#### Storage progress and recovery

The default receipt archive budget is 16 MiB, configurable from 4–64 MiB, with at most 128 sealed epochs. The admission budget includes archived, pending and write-scratch bytes, and reserves room before a remote append. Metadata has its own 1 MiB per-file bound. These are application admission limits, not an OS disk quota or protection against unrelated writers.

At the default 60-second cadence, continuous new rows may reach the epoch-count limit in roughly two hours, earlier if the byte limit is reached. The worker preserves existing receipts, pauses sealing and reports the hold. It does not delete originals, silently start a new history or block protection startup. Review/export and controlled archive lifecycle management require explicit operator handling; automatic long-term rollover is not provided in this version.

Each capture is limited to 4,096 rows and 16 MiB of row data; larger valid batches are split into bounded prefixes. Historical verification checks up to 10 ranges per cycle with a cooperative five-second local-work budget. Cached status shows the sealed tip, archive use, pending commit, verification backlog, known missing rows and latest changed rows. A completed cycle does not mean every historic row was checked during that cycle. Supplementary SQLite runtime limits are used where available; mandatory bounded SQL projections also apply on supported Python versions without that API.

A durable pending claim precedes the remote append. On reply loss or failed local finalization, restart reconciles only that exact claim with a fresh signed authority head. Unexpected ahead/behind/forked state, missing archives, corrupt metadata and unexplained scratch are preserved and held for review. There is no automatic baseline reset, key replacement or evidence repair.

Closing Settings detaches its view. The runtime still owns an admitted credential task and drains it on STOP. Both that task and the recorder reader must actually retire before their storage/custody is released. Uncertain native cleanup retains its owner and cannot claim successful replacement.

#### Freshness limits

Archived signatures alone are historical authenticity, not proof of the current authority head. Production requests require pinned HTTPS, fresh signed nonce-bound responses and a remote response continuity floor. That floor is outside the monitored host's snapshot boundary; it is not a local counter file. Rollback of the authority's own entire trusted root still needs independent generation-floor or hardware protection. A response sequence floor alone is not a permanent incident latch or proof against every authority rollback.

The separate TPM verification library requires authenticated physical-device enrollment and a protected external writer. It is not automatically deployed or substituted for a missing witness. See the 1.15 release scope for the other hardening layers and their remaining deployment requirements.

### Managed vulnerable driver policy

Angerona 1.15 includes an installed-service path for preparing, approving and applying a reviewed driver deny policy. Source Observe has no enrollment or elevation shortcut. The default response-service v1 provisioning remains diagnostic-only. Only an explicitly provisioned v2 profile can register the native policy executor.

The implemented profile is an unsigned, removable multiple-policy base deny policy. Its checks constrain kernel driver denials while preserving the required user-mode allow rules. It does not activate HVCI, change Secure Boot, install a kernel driver or remove arbitrary Windows policies. Local administrators can tamper with an unsigned policy; boot audit fallback and reboot requirements remain part of deployment review.

#### Fixed enrollment

A signed installed package, immutable publisher pins, actual SCM registration, restricted service token, native administration rights and protected data/key custody are prerequisites. Installation must supply exact angerona.response-service.provisioning.v2 provisioning with the own-unsigned-multiple-policy profile and its pinned manifest hash.

The fixed service root is native ProgramData's Angerona/ResponseBroker/DriverPolicy. The profile references reviewed local material IDs and pinned artifacts: the manifest, catalog, XML, compiled CIP, compatibility reports and fixed native-tool hashes/publishers. Separate private broker, journal, capability and transport keys stay under service custody. Downloaded blocklists, arbitrary caller paths, script text and GUI claims do not enroll authority. Review the actual service composition and host admission.

#### Audit approval enforcement and removal

The online guide includes this workflow diagram; Figure 6 shows the combined 1.15 hardening layers.

The requester prepares a server-owned plan and receives its proposal digest. Two other enrolled OS users independently sign the exact approval purpose. The requester can then request execution. Enforce mode requires the previous audit evidence, elapsed review window and separately pinned compatibility and recovery review. Removal requires its own approved plan and proof of the exact owned unsigned policy. Signed/UEFI-locked policy removal is unavailable.

The closed IPC operations are driver.status, driver.prepare, driver.approve, driver.execute, driver.poll and driver.cancel. Prepare/approve/execute queue onto one retained service worker and immediately return opaque job IDs; polling reads bounded cached results. The native pipe captures the Windows peer identity. Requests cannot supply a replacement peer, executor, credential verifier, native guard or raw policy. Each request, including polling/cancellation, rechecks the pinned provisioning generation and current enrollment. A changed profile requires controlled service review and restart, rather than silent authority replacement.

Cancellation fences future work. It cannot undo a native change that already committed. An interrupted or uncertain operation requires reconciliation with the durable intent journal and actual native configuration before retrying. The runtime bounds its plan and job caches to 64 entries each; capacity holds require operator review rather than unbounded cache growth.

#### Configuration receipts and remaining acceptance

configured means the admitted backend or an exact native configuration postcondition was observed in its stated scope. The service always reports kernel\_prevention\_verified: false. Configuration readback alone does not prove a driver was blocked, remove an already loaded driver, restore stripped callbacks, verify telemetry, or prove reboot compatibility. Actual Windows build-specific audit/enforce/reboot/removal testing belongs in a disposable signed-installation acceptance environment.

The native paths retain process/job, file, pipe, OVERLAPPED, event, buffer and peer/token/SCM handle owners. STOP cancels queued work and requires real retirement before releasing custody. Unknown completion or close results keep their owners and fence replacement; they cannot become successful cleanup receipts. This implementation does not grant ELAM/PPL protection or immunity to an administrator or kernel compromise.

Source updates do not activate host enforcement. Signed installation, native rights, enrollment, ConfigCI availability, independent approvals and clean-VM acceptance remain required.

## 17 Current operator workflows for version 1 15

Current source guidance as of 9 November 2026. The public application version remains 1.15.0. Historical tests and dated implementation versions later in this manual retain their original scope. Fresh runtime, full repository tests, hosted checks and accepted signed deployment require their own evidence.

### 17 1 Read the dashboard and choose a working posture

Angerona is a local endpoint detection and response (EDR), network detection and response (NDR), and security orchestration automation and response (SOAR) workbench. It joins conditional sensors, evidence review and scoped response. A source checkout normally starts without administrator rights in Observe and development mode; the accepted signed installation is a separate deployment boundary.

Start with the assessment banner, current alerts and collector coverage. Enabled is a saved selection, running is a worker lifecycle, health is a module report, and assurance describes tested prerequisites. A running idle SOAR worker can correctly show that response policy is disabled. Open its inspector instead of treating green worker health as permission or proof of prevention. Chill's held count describes selected startup work deferred by the current pause intent. Selected checkboxes stay enabled, and checks already in flight may finish.

Module Health starts collapsed; other dashboard panels open to fit the window. The title, posture and Current Assessment sit above one action row. STOP stays fixed at the right while the other controls scroll horizontally on narrow windows; Tab reveals the focused control. Supported work windows can remain open together and minimize or maximize. Optional motion cannot consume or duplicate an action.

Function accents identify monitoring and inspection in blue, analysis and research in violet, configuration and recovery in amber, and controlled response in red. Labels, severity colors, coverage warnings and permission checks retain their own meaning. Secondary help and provenance expand on demand while progress, findings and primary controls remain visible.

Tray and orb restore show the real Qt dashboard before optional animation. If a paint is not observed, two bounded presentation attempts include a plain restore with owned effects retired. A nonmodal notice offers Retry display, normal Safe STOP and instructions. Fixed private diagnostics and at most 16 memory records explain the attempt. No external recovery child, settings reset or engine-policy change occurs; a Qt paint is not readable-pixel or protection proof.

The EKG strip requires advancing authenticated progress from the exact observed process generation. A stale or unavailable source flatlines red. A pulse shows recent liveness, not complete telemetry or a clean host. GUI lag samples and a native stack ending in the Qt event loop do not establish a deadlock by themselves.

Black Box freezes the complete health-table display, including source dates and duplicate rows. Unchanged rows avoid repeated item allocation and sorting; hidden views defer rendering until shown. Changed rows preserve selection and scroll position. Invalid or failed refreshes remain visible as gaps; this optimization does not identify the cause of an earlier GUI pause.

Use Notifications to review deferred prompts without blocking the dashboard. Select or open an item for its existing review controls. A deferred removable-device prompt is not consent to trust, unlock or scan that device. Device identity and PIN checks remain separate. STOP or tray Quit records deliberate shutdown and fences automatic peer relaunch; an uncertain owned child remains explicitly unresolved until its retirement is proven.

DEMO only. Compact dashboard with Current Assessment above one action row and a fixed STOP control. Synthetic records perform no host actions.

### 17 2 Complete setup and optional settings

Full Setup and Settings expose operating posture, storage and recovery, local AI, response policy, external tools, rules, diagnostics and optional integrations. Review defaults before enabling a feature. The complete settings reference records code defaults, not the current user's saved preferences or proof that a collector can run on this platform.

Community YARA rules and community SOAR playbooks have separate global runtime switches and both default off. Individually importing, testing or activating a draft does not enable either switch. Save through the tool settings view; a failed background save preserves prior preferences and restores the visible saved switch state.

The administrator option defaults off. An operator enables it and accepts the operating system prompt for that session. Elevation does not bypass an unenrolled backend, grant kernel protection or make every listed module operational. Keep credentials in protected stores and review the warning beneath each authority-related option.

Settings code sandboxes open separate editable copies. Saving or resetting a copy does not rewrite installed Core, silently activate imported code or bypass signed release/source review. Record intentional custom changes so update or recovery review can preserve them.

### 17 3 Suggested community tools and editable copies

Open the GitHub icon for Curated scanners, Source Library and analysis, Suggested tools, Rules and Playbooks, and Settings. Select an entry to read its upstream link, exact pinned revision, adapter capability, excluded behavior and credits. An adapter integrates a defined subset; the presence of Caldera, Velociraptor or Wazuh does not install their whole platforms or enroll another host.

Zero-Breach is the maintained pinned scanner. Atomic Red Team supplies compatible metadata mapped to reviewed controls; its arbitrary attack commands and prerequisites are not run. Sigma matching accepts only the supported logsource, fields, modifiers and conditions. Sysmon Modular supports configuration review. YARA-X uses the existing pinned engine for supported inert-buffer checks. External result adapters remain advisory and cannot grant response authority.

Import public HTTPS GitHub source at an immutable commit, inspect its files and licenses, and explicitly review that exact import. Install selected prepares only its supported integration. Run self-check checks the stated adapter and fixtures; it does not certify a host scan. Uninstall preserves reports, source imports, editable copies and preferences. Explicit Zero-Breach uninstall intent prevents automatic preparation from undoing that decision until an explicit restore.

Create editable copy opens a bounded working copy. Save copy, Show diff, Revert selected copy and Validate or analyze data affect that copy. This source sandbox is not an operating system isolation boundary. Editing a script does not execute it or replace the managed scanner. VM analysis is a separate backend with its own prerequisites, quotas and retained worker custody; current VMware acceptance remains held at its documented configuration-custody boundary.

Upstream references and licensing context: [Zero-Breach Toolkit](https://github.com/interplains/zero-breach-toolkit), [Atomic Red Team](https://github.com/redcanaryco/atomic-red-team), [SigmaHQ](https://github.com/SigmaHQ/sigma), [Sysmon Modular](https://github.com/olafhartong/sysmon-modular), [YARA-X](https://github.com/virustotal/yara-x), [Apache Caldera](https://github.com/apache/caldera), [Velociraptor](https://github.com/Velocidex/velociraptor), and [Wazuh](https://github.com/wazuh/wazuh). Retain the selected pinned source and its own license; project inclusion is not an endorsement or complete platform integration.

### 17 4 Build YARA rules and SOAR tactics

Open Rules and Playbooks for an X/O tactics board, guided builder, source discovery, draft editor and result details. The board explains input, validation, policy and response paths. It is a planning visualization, not an enforcement receipt.

Choose a predefined source or a public HTTPS GitHub URL, fetch a pinned catalog, review the source and check compatible entries. Batch install creates drafts. Foreign workflow JSON, analyzers and Python, PowerShell or shell scripts remain inert when they do not match Angerona's supported schema. Per-item licenses remain part of the review.

Save draft preserves a separate revision. Validate checks syntax, source binding and supported schema; Sample test tests that exact draft. A checkmark requires the expected positive and negative sample outcomes where such fixtures are defined. Compilation alone is not detection accuracy. Read the red X or held reason instead of substituting a green indicator.

Activate validated and Rollback compile the complete candidate YARA set in a bounded ordinary-user owned helper before commit, then recheck current source review. Separate namespaces avoid name replacement. Raw source and compile-input hashes remain distinct. Compatible YARA excludes includes and imported modules; the current aggregate is limited to 32 sources and 64 KiB.

Compatible declarative SOAR uses the closed angerona-playbook/v1 JSON schema for notification or a containment request. Original evidence, opt-in, corroboration, exact-target and Combat gates remain in force. Disable removes one item's routing while retaining revisions; turning its global switch off stops new routing of that kind. Rollback cannot bypass source revocation, validation or response policy.
