### 17 5 Use the standalone Red Team application

The dashboard Red Team button opens a separate ordinary-user application with the existing campaign, progress, history and after-action workflow. Core retains prepared plans, enrolled detectors, validation leases, signed reports and response policy. Closing the tool is not a Core shutdown, and watchdog recovery does not silently relaunch this explicitly started tool.

A separate tool launch failure now retains a private phase/error-type receipt and a notification with a modeless startup review. Retry tool requires the same current owner to be fully retired and repeats source-seal, owned-Job and authenticated-IPC checks. Closing review preserves the receipt; no sensor or response policy is changed to force a launch.

The separate tool shares a 90-second bootstrap deadline beginning before Core's source check and inherited unchanged by the child. Both source checks and authenticated native admission remain required. After initialization, the first Qt paint has 15 seconds within a 105-second whole-startup cap. Source sealing checks the deadline and STOP cancellation between bounded operations. An observed cancellation, expiry or invalid clock cannot produce a verified seal; a known negative source-change receipt stays preserved. Cooperative checks cannot interrupt native I/O that is already blocked.

Open Simulation setup to adjust profiles, intensity, marker location and custom inert markers. The current target, containment readiness, overall wheel, result bar, verdict and Launch and Stop controls remain visible while setup is folded. Collapsing setup preserves selections and never changes response authority.

Private authenticated directional IPC binds the current parent, launcher and actual child process generations. Queued UI requests retain that owner epoch. Process probes use fixed inert commands; marker writes receive permission for one newly created Core-owned file. Repository code and child-selected paths are not execution authority. Exact Job ownership covers actual descendants on Windows.

The progress wheel and caught versus missed bar describe the current validated workflow; the pass/fail badge follows those scoped results. Open diagnostic detail for each outcome, its detector observation, response receipt and coverage gap. An empty response queue alone cannot finish a session: the admitted detector must complete a fresh cycle, followed by a fresh response-queue observation under the original deadline.

A failed report-integrity check keeps the immutable after-action report unavailable until genuine evidence loads. Cleanup does not manufacture detection or response credit. A practice marker, its name or its content does not make a live unregistered object safe; only an exact enrolled inert target can receive the scoped practice exception. Catch percentages must not be presented as an independently measured real-world detection rate.

### 17 6 Navigate the three dimensional Suite Map

SUITE MAP 3D is a software-drawn local view of Core, EventBus, modules, companions, cached mounted volumes, host-visible peripheral functions and retained observed endpoints. Scroll to zoom, drag to orbit, Shift-drag to pan, hover or select for details, and use Take me there to reach the owning existing controls. Filters, search, animation and Reset view aid navigation.

Bright links describe observed publications or endpoint metadata; dashed links describe architecture. Moving particles do not prove subscriber delivery, recorder persistence, an active socket or a blocked attack. Cached health is not a liveness attestation. The view discloses event losses, omitted nodes, source age and unavailable inventories.

A displayed drive is not automatically trusted or scanned. Navigate to the existing device review and retain its consent and PIN boundary. Unmounted storage and firmware or cable implants invisible to the operating system cannot be invented by the map. Rendering stops while hidden or closed; existing cached data avoids GUI-thread host scans.

### 17 7 Spyware Scan and attached device review

SpywareGuard keeps research/news first, then progress and reported hits, current task/file/timing, and cached computer information with separately labeled scanner usage and permissions. The red Spyware Scan control defaults to Entire PC; open Scan setup to change scope and included checks. Recent native records are separate from this scan's findings or a confirmed breach. Overall and per-reader progress have different meanings; file completion requires a supplied count. Unknown ETA or current file remains unknown.

Native SpywareGuard checks and Zero-Breach are separate coverage sources. Missing permissions, readers, deadline expiry, cancellation or retained incomplete reports must remain visible in the after-action result. No listed findings after incomplete coverage is not a clean-PC result. Investigate, trace, patch, isolate or kill controls require their own supported target, evidence, policy and privilege; report text is not that authority.

Unlimited report count removes the slot-count limit only. Byte, inventory and free-space budgets still protect storage. Existing reports are retained when a new admission is held; export and verify before explicitly removing originals. Startup scratch pressure should leave the recovery interface available, with detailed diagnostics, rather than silently deleting evidence or pretending the engine started.

Optional research downloads use configured HTTPS sources and disclose live-fetch age or failure separately from bundled reference briefs. Feed details expands the article summary and source checks. A rotating banner does not make a stale brief current. Attached storage and peripherals use host-visible metadata and supported scan readers. Suspicion or an opaque accessory is not proof of a hidden hardware implant.

### 17 8 Telemetry continuity forensic evidence and local analysis

Provider-specific benign canaries require a native ETW or Sysmon echo with the current collection generation and authenticated durable evidence. A general heartbeat or polling echo cannot satisfy that native proof. Current ETWR publishes process-start events; native DLL and network ETW coverage is not supplied by enabling that one provider path. Sysmon image, network and DNS coverage remains conditional on its actual installation and configuration.

AMSI Bridge inspects already observed script text. It accepts the bounded ETWR cmdline alias and explicit supported text fields; this is not a registered global AMSI provider or pre-execution interception. The unstable native in-process compatibility option stays off by default. A real malicious AMSI API verdict can carry already authenticated native ETWR PID, raw FILETIME, image and source proof only after checking the same bytes before and after scanning.

That positive finding can enter separately opted-in forensic capture without granting process-response authority. Missing, stale, remote, drill, lossy or changed provenance preserves the critical content observation but holds automatic capture. No current-PID lookup substitutes for missing historical birth. Legacy active detectors without original raw FILETIME still leave this forensic path unavailable.

Forensics retains an exact noninheritable native read/query process handle across bounded strings and owner-PID socket capture. It excludes protected system, Windows, self and Angerona targets. This is bounded evidence extraction, not a full process dump. AES-GCM frames, a random case key wrapped for the current user, authenticated terminal receipts and file/directory identity checks protect copied evidence at rest. Explicit operator export to a new directory is the only plaintext path.

Finite clocks, deadlines, capacity and complete writes are checked. A failed frame encryption or write permanently poisons that writer: later append or terminal receipt calls cannot reuse the consumed AEAD nonce, and partial ciphertext remains without a valid completion claim. Ambiguous native close retains the exact owner and never retries its possibly recycled handle number. Further forensic capture is held until Core restart; other modules and normal STOP are not held for a file/process handle owned by Core. Current-user DPAPI and Python key handling do not defeat same-user or kernel compromise or guarantee RAM erasure.

Native Sysmon DNS records now reach the lexical decoder through its source checks. Beacon cadence uses parsed addresses, PID birth and explicit continuity epochs; stable sockets and incomplete snapshots cannot fabricate repeat callbacks. These lexical/timing observations remain leads unless the existing separate corroboration and response conditions are met.

SentinelLens is a bounded advisory read model. It normalizes supported imports, links anomaly evidence and explains possible next steps without executing remediation. Accepted queue work drains before stop; a failed builder retains its prior snapshot, retries, and discloses an unpublished suffix instead of claiming a clean flush. Imported data and graph proximity do not establish live source authenticity or malicious causation.

### 17 9 Signal optional integration and shutdown

Mobile Response Bridge remains separately opted in. It requires the configured exact native executable hash/publisher, account/operator identity and protected PIN. Commands retain sender, freshness, replay, one-use token and action scope checks. A local CLI invocation receipt does not prove Signal connectivity or recipient delivery, and a version self-test makes no such claim.

A full invocation lease covers executable preflight, the fixed system Authenticode helper, the CLI operation and final executable-pin close. The child begins suspended, enters its owned Job, then runs. Output readers, native process/tree signals and closes are checked before a result can be verified. Unknown retirement preserves exact resources, fences further Signal launches and remains visible to Core shutdown; no process-name search or foreign target grants ownership.

An unproven external tree prevents a false completed STOP receipt. A file-close-only reference after its tree and reader are proven retired holds this optional capability without blocking global restart forever. Failed notifications remain in a bounded retry digest; sending a digest cannot erase newer arrivals or mint replacement response permissions. No live Signal send, inbox or recipient acknowledgement was exercised by the documented offline review.

### 17 10 Adaptation recovery and preserved custom changes

Auto Adapt separates audit, a golden baseline, proposed exact changes, explicit approval, native readback and supported rollback. The change list and activity history explain what was proposed and what actually happened. Adjust scope before approval, then inspect receipts and residual drift. Unelevated firewall access-denied results are a visible prerequisite gap, not a reason to widen every module's authority.

Source peers bind heartbeat counters to exact native invocation generations and stop advancing when supervision work exceeds its deadline. Source seals hold changed peers without silently overwriting intentional edits. GitHub repair uses the existing verified Safe Startup boundary and preserved originals. The 48-file recovery profile needs an explicit reviewed transition from an older updater that understands only the former 39-file profile.

Canonical Windows storage derives from the actual process token so a helper's private USERPROFILE cannot redirect update/recovery roots. Reserved background helpers preserve failure exits and custody diagnostics without foreground MessageBoxes. An interactive failed launch still explains recovery; unknown source, ownership or authority must not be bypassed merely to paint a trusted-looking protection state.

Public GitHub update checks default to their saved opt-in and prompt before installation. Download into staging, inspect source changes and custom additions, preserve settings, and activate through the reviewed update path. Source version 1.15.0 is not a new signed installed binary. Signed release signing, privileged service enrollment, native policy and hardware/witness acceptance remain their own deployments.

### 17 11 Individual module tests and supported recovery

Self-Test reports each module's own diagnostic and sample limits. Read the positive/negative fixture, unavailable dependency or permission, expected postcondition and actual result. A generic lifecycle check cannot substitute for observing the module's security job, and a mock provider result cannot establish a live provider.

Bounded module workers and spare test slots let other eligible modules proceed while a slow test uses its own budget. A timeout remains incomplete or failed for that scope; it does not turn the whole session into an automatic pass or authorize an unsafe retry. The stored per-module time budget is separate from native custody and OS limits.

Self-Test settings expose module-specific guidance, test code and separate editable copies. Automatic supported recovery is restricted to the explicitly selected module list; its code default is empty. Re-test and inspect the exact result after a supported repair. Do not clear alerts, replace evidence baselines or hot-load arbitrary code to make a result green.

The complete module reference links every declared dedicated test for inspection. Supported repair guidance is conditional on the module and current manager generation; it is not a universal automatic patch engine or permission to bypass disabled policy, missing native collectors or unenrolled privilege.

### Threat scenarios and the expected review path

#### Office document creates a script host

Preserve native parent/child and script text, correlate available sources and examine the exact alert. A lexical or graph marker is a lead; supported corroborated active evidence may request Combat. Post-observation text inspection does not prove that execution was prevented.

#### A signed vulnerable driver may blind telemetry

Inspect provenance, OS policy state and independent native canary gaps. A live worker can be deaf. Enrolled WDAC/HVCI prevention is conditional; no source-mode kernel immunity or intact-callback attestation exists.

#### A flagged executable changes during containment

Retain native process/file/ancestor leases through intent, dispatch and postcondition or hold the action. Path firewall success does not prove PID-bound socket admission or established/inherited-flow teardown.

#### A newly attached device is suspicious

Use Notifications and device review, validate identity and supported coverage, and keep consent/PIN and response gates. Host metadata cannot establish hidden cable firmware behavior. A displayed device is not a completed scan.

#### A verified breach requests network lockdown

Native breach qualification and the existing opted-in authority decide whether a managed containment request can proceed. Review critical evidence and receipts; Lift Lockdown restores only managed changes. An imported report or dramatic red UI is not proof or a new firewall grant.

#### An attacker replays old local state

Local integrity alone cannot establish whole-root freshness. An independently enrolled witness or hardware-backed floor must be available and bound to admission. OS servicing/version observations are partial evidence and do not replace vendor security updates.

Individual test: [Open source](https://github.com/Ag3nt47/AngeronaSuite/blob/main/src/angerona/modules/storage_hygiene.py#L472). Verify detection/proposal and that execution/deletion remain retired.

### Sysmon Event Bridge

Reads the current Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational event range and emits them onto the Angerona bus. Falls back to psutil process-diff when Sysmon or win32evtlog is unavailable.

Category: Endpoint. Source: [Open source](https://github.com/Ag3nt47/AngeronaSuite/blob/main/src/angerona/modules/sysmon_listener.py#L304).

Individual test: [Open source](https://github.com/Ag3nt47/AngeronaSuite/blob/main/src/angerona/modules/sysmon_listener.py#L1338). This module declares a dedicated self-test. Inspect the method for its sample, limits and asserted postconditions.

### Telemetry Canary Drills

Fires synthetic benign canary subprocesses at regular intervals and listens for the corresponding ETWG 4688 echo on the EventBus.  A missed canary reports an availability gap with unconfirmed cause; repeated misses on a previously verified path retain CRITICAL priority.

Category: Resilience. Source: [Open source](https://github.com/Ag3nt47/AngeronaSuite/blob/main/src/angerona/modules/canary_drill.py#L117).

Individual test: [Open source](https://github.com/Ag3nt47/AngeronaSuite/blob/main/src/angerona/modules/canary_drill.py#L884). Verify contracts and reject self/untrusted echoes before ETWG smoke-test.

## 20 Complete interface control reference

This index covers all 735 declared control sites across the GUI sources: buttons, actions, toggles, options, tabs and menus. Shared builders and generated labels can produce more than one live control. The descriptions define the action family; the linked line identifies its exact implementation and contextual scope. Current selections, dynamic labels, unavailable providers and separate authority warnings must be read in the actual view. This inventory is not a claim that every optional integration is deployed.

### Current source maintenance and preview limits

Alert-table resize work is coalesced and unchanged measurements are reused; this does not establish the cause or resolution of an earlier GUI delay. Red Team preserves typed startup failures, transports nonempty history through strict JSON, checks process-supplier snapshots with an explicit clock, and fits its first normal window to available frame/client space. Full readiness, warnings and Launch/Stop remain fixed while tall content scrolls; later operator geometry is preserved. Known completed native-reader work contributes to scan workflow progress without changing raw stage counts, unknowns or coverage gaps, and without a monotonic clamp. Full-budget header captions now preserve their complete text with fractional font widths. A known ready, unbound Spyware view shows the selected next-run budget rather than a generic status timer; bound and unknown timing is preserved.

The initial Combat termination lease receives the original issuer-enrolled canary proof explicitly. Fresh native generation, image, parent, Job, lease, prepared-plan and original-contract checks remain mandatory at later barriers. This admits only the exact enrolled inert target in Source Observe; it does not grant general host Protect authority or response credit for natural target expiry.

A measured pre-worker working-space hold leaves optional Zero-Breach not started while the exact native request can finish independently. Optional working admission remains 3 GiB plus the configured allowance, which defaults to 256 MiB. Unlimited report count does not waive byte, inventory or free-space limits. STOP, deadlines, generation changes and unknown custody retain strict retirement paths.

This source preview retains the genuine Shark T1041 outbound network-containment gap. A controlled detection, marker-contract recognition, path-firewall observation or successful tool launch is not proof of blocked exfiltration, native analytic coverage or established and inherited socket teardown.

Current controlled Red Team observation: A fresh authenticated APT-only run verified 37/37 controlled containment checks. The three T1059 probes were bound to their original native generations and committed retained-handle exit postconditions before their fixed 30-second natural deadline; the original ledger verified 11/11 HMAC records without gaps. Native-analytic credit was 0/37. The finding contract remains open. This proves that controlled run and its per-target actions, not a general malware catch rate; the earlier Partial36/37 result remains preserved.

Current native and optional-tool scan observation: One Entire PC workflow finished in 47:49 within its one-hour budget, with one Start and unchanged saved preferences. Native completed in 14.5 seconds with definition, memory, configured-bound and permission gaps. Zero-Breach ran for 47:43 and returned findings (exit 2), not a timeout; all five readers retained unchecked areas. File fingerprints skipped 1,119 candidates (379 permission denials, 663 unreadable, 31 above 120 MB, 46 cloud-only); browser locks/reparse roots, disabled online/DNS verification and restricted Startup data remain gaps. Prefetch/Amcache admitted zero artifacts: UNKNOWN execution coverage, not a passed collector. One 29 August historical HSTS contact trace overlaps the native advisory, with two contextual references; these do not prove infection/execution or grant response authority. Complete upstream size/SHA-256 matched the controller receipt; the controller copy is a bounded projection, not independent cryptographic authentication. No response or alert clearing was performed.

Final shutdown and saved-preference review: Fresh actual default windows fit the observed 1920×1032 work area without resize/maximize: Main showed full STOP/SELF-TEST captions; ready Spyware showed its selected one-hour budget, with no generic 300-second elapsed label. A prior default normal Red Team window had full readiness and Launch/Stop. No new drill or scan was started for these UI checks. Final normal STOP exited 0; 13 held original native generations signaled with unchanged identity and once-closed handles, 12 runtime source anchors were released, and all 161 saved preferences were byte-identical. Three earlier snapshot-only transients were not independently witnessed at exit; they are not counted among the 13 retained generations. Earlier 13/11 and 16/12 shutdown receipts remain separate historical scopes.

Source and hosted validation: Combat: 252 passed, one expected skip, two deselected; 24 new cases included. Storage: 162 passed, one private-harness inert-child denial, seven deselected; 15 new passed. Only the denied existing node was rerun after its exact allowlist correction and passed unchanged. Private header 81/81 and scan 64/64 gates plus canonical caption/idle 30/30 passed; scopes overlap. Latest Ruff and in-memory syntax passed for 1,581 files/27,924,607 bytes, zero missing/failed; before/after hashes matched 3c697a67aa516c73dec5aef957ad8fc8fbc79b8bf8735c809737e60f51f7f81d. Both diff scopes and unchanged 48-input recovery-manifest/bootstrap checks passed. Original historical harness failures remain retained. Prepublication checkpoint (9 November 2026): reviewed manual/media/export checks, guarded publication and all required exact-commit GitHub Actions are separate delivery gates (https://github.com/Ag3nt47/AngeronaSuite/actions); this source record does not attest later hosted CI.

### 21 1 v1 10 2 loop disposition

- Research ranked current open-source and standards gaps without claiming parity. Built items are separated from proposals.

### 21 2 Automatic Red Team validation correction 2026 08 25

A live Extreme GUI campaign exposed a launch-contract defect: Auto-contain armed the response tier but did not activate Purple Guard's fixed simulation detector pack. The report therefore recorded only 4/52 eligible detections. This was a real validation-path failure, not acceptable detector latency.

- Corrected launch behavior: an Auto-contain Red Team run activates all 13 reviewed simulation-only technique signatures before the first marker is created. Activation preserves earlier signed candidate lineage and fails closed if the pack cannot be persisted.

- Scope remains exact: the pack recognizes only inert \_redteam\_\* artifacts in the dedicated or explicitly registered drill target and nonce-tagged idle processes. It does not convert suspicious filenames elsewhere into host-wide threat authority.

- AAR correlation now prefers the exact Adversary Combat receipt with a verified postcondition over an earlier delegation wrapper. A real verified Combat receipt counts as both an applied action contract and a closure.

- The first corrected live round achieved 52/52 detection but only 51/52 response and 12/13 closure, so the validator rejected it and automatically continued.

- The second round, run redteam-1787697587-bf119f, achieved 52/52 detection, 52/52 automatic response, 13/13 action contracts, 13/13 verified closure, and a passing no-false-alert resilience control. Average detection was 0.57 seconds and average mitigation was 1.09 seconds.

- Post-run cleanup verified 223 authenticated action records, zero active reversible actions, an empty journal error, zero recovery requirements, zero remaining drill markers, and zero tagged probe processes.

- Regression evidence: 1,257 tests passed with three intentional platform skips; 308 Python files compiled; repository-wide Ruff checks passed; the headless application self-check passed 26/26; and 128 adversary-boundary negative controls passed before the live campaign.

Interpretation limit: this proves 100% end-to-end handling of the defined 13-class, 52-step inert campaign. It is not a claim that any finite product detects every possible real-world threat.

### Operator update 8 October 2026

Benign Shark and Red Team simulations continue when automatic response is unavailable. An amber warning remains visible through progress and results. Selected profiles, intensity and inert process/file exercises still run. Target ownership, the validation lease and engine startup must still succeed. Only authenticated verified response receipts count as containment; a completed exercise with no receipts remains unverified.

Adversary Combat already defaults to automatic standing authority. Eligible detector evidence invokes the saved file, process, network, host-isolation and deception rules without asking for each incident and without requiring Ollama. The policy is restricted to exact authenticated detector-authorized targets. Health findings, exposure and model advice do not become containment commands.

The footer shows Auto ARMED, HELD, OFF, STARTING or UNAVAILABLE beside posture. Settings \> Adversary Combat describes the effective rules and retains readiness, verified action history and Undo. Contain mode suspends eligible processes even if a different process action is saved. An armed policy cannot guarantee that every alert has an eligible target or that every action succeeds.

A narrowly defined interrupted simulation checkpoint can now recover automatically during enabled Combat startup. Recovery requires an authenticated journal with exactly one trailing quarantine intent, agreeing protected checkpoint and independent witness, and no ambiguous pending recovery. The original single-link marker must retain its recorded identity, hash and exact shipped comprehensive-drill bytes in the suite drill sandbox; its quarantine destination must be absent.

Recovery preserves private, verified copies of the unchanged journal, protected store and witness before advancing the matching checkpoint. It neither moves the marker nor creates signing authority, truncates history or reports a quarantine success. Normal reconciliation records the unapplied intent. Changed files, real containment effects, unrelated files, unsupported history or an unsuccessful proof leave automatic response held for verified recovery.

When restarting this Windows source installation, use kill-all-angerona.bat with elevation to stop the verified Angerona processes, then reopen start-angerona.bat in the normal user session. The source launcher intentionally runs unelevated in Observe/development mode; the separately installed signed distribution supplies Windows Protect boundaries. Do not delete recovery data to clear a warning.

Package installation pins PySide6 6.11.1, the validated GUI runtime; 6.12.0 remains unsupported after native CI crashes. The implementation record, regression evidence and remaining limits are in [analysis/unattended-response-2026-10-08.md](../analysis/unattended-response-2026-10-08.md). Earlier validation totals in this manual retain their historical dates. GitHub Actions and the guarded publisher establish the exact published commit and current CI outcome.

### Operator update 9 October 2026

Simulation preparation and stop cleanup now run outside the dashboard event loop. The console shows preparation while target checks, detector readiness and engine startup complete. Keep the console open to see the handoff. Stop clean cancels pending preparation and retires the run it owns; a cleanup failure remains visible. Duplicate launches wait for preparation or cleanup to finish. Selected exercises and response rules retain their existing behavior.

The October 9 comprehensive campaign recorded 27 of 80 planned mandatory steps before a validation-producer liveness failure. Its manifest is incomplete and ineligible for scoring. Executed steps are not detections or containment receipts. No finalized October 9 after-action report was available during review; the September 23 report is historical. Live producer and signed-evidence checks remain required, and the failed producer has not been identified from the generic error.

Repeated BYOVD drill phases now use distinct inert marker paths. This prevents a marker from an earlier phase blocking a later exclusive creation. Detector matching accepts the exact generated name, while response eligibility still requires the registered file identity and content. A similar filename alone grants no authority. Worker-start failure also releases Shark's run state so a later attempt can start.

Black Box refreshes firewall and SOAR snapshots in background workers and retains the prior view if a refresh fails. SOAR shows at most 200 valid records from the latest 1 MiB. CPU readings now retain a sample for the same process identity.

Cancellation remains interruptible, deadlines still apply and partial inventories do not become completed coverage. Driver inventory has a finite watchdog budget matching its collector timeout; routine network-trust inventory can wait longer under pressure while collecting fresh evidence.

Source files are limited to 4 MiB; undo retains at most 20 copies and 16 MiB. Trusted baseline tests have bounded child output, memory and cleanup. Candidate edits remain AST-only. This editor is not an isolation boundary for executing hostile code, and working copies do not replace production sources.

Flow windows cancel the initial AI poll when closing and reject late worker updates. These changes address confirmed blocking and lifetime bugs; they do not guarantee a maximum response time under Windows load. Restart Angerona and Black Box to load the update. ### All requested security integrations belong to v1 14

The v1.14 scope includes verified readiness, an independent witness, privilege separation, authenticated approvals, process-bound network admission, identity and browser producers, guided prevention, independent recovery and release trust with efficacy evaluation. The current acceptance register is [docs/releases/v1.14-security-integration.md](../docs/releases/v1.14-security-integration.md). It distinguishes tested implementations, ongoing integration and independently provisioned deployment requirements. Publication follows observation and bug fixes; a version label or declared feature does not establish working enforcement.

ATT&CK Coverage now shows declared, collecting, detection-tested and response-verified stages. Collection requires a current registered sensor generation, completed fresh work, health of at least 90 and no unknown or reported event overflow. Stopping or replacing a producer withdraws its readiness. Scoped detection proof expires after 24 hours and response proof after one hour; clock discontinuities withdraw proof. A practice marker and its verified cleanup prove that bounded control only, not the real exploit or every technique mapped to the detector. The tested-coverage percentage is separate from the declaration count.

UGCAP \> Independent Witness provides opt-in enrollment and cached status for a separately administered private HTTPS witness. Its fixed endpoint must end /v1/ugcap-witness. Explicitly provision the host signing identity, exchange public enrollment and mTLS information with the separate administrator, and enroll the exact TLS leaf certificate pin plus witness Ed25519 PUBLIC PEM. Private PKI and separate host/witness signing-key roles remain required. The [tools/ugcap\_witness\_server.py](../tools/ugcap_witness_server.py) --initialize operation creates first retained state explicitly; ordinary restart cannot silently reset missing state. No external witness is deployed or configured by this update.

Applying witness settings or provisioning a host key invalidates cached assurance. Attach the enrolled vault, supply its passcode AND fresh required TPM-backed hardware proof, then complete a full UGCAP Verify now cycle. Only a fresh authenticated local checkpoint and matching enrolled witness receipt can satisfy the gate. Check witness now subsequently heartbeats an already verified checkpoint; it cannot initialize, advance, reset or reconcile a retained head. Missing or stale required witness evidence keeps the workspace held. No passcode or source contents are transmitted.

An intentional golden-baseline or vault identity change also requires separately administered witness enrollment or reconciliation. Do not disable a required witness, delete existing state or reset its head merely to obtain green status. Checkpoints expose an old valid host snapshot against an unchanged independent witness; rollback of the entire witness appliance still requires a further independent freshness floor.

Authenticated approval proofs bind an exact operation digest, a short lifetime, a nonce and an enrolled issuer/subject/key identity. Multiple labels for one operator or key do not supply multiple independent approvals. Durable revocations and pre-execution attempt records prevent stale or uncertain actions from being replayed; independent postcondition failure is recorded as verification failure. These checks govern explicitly integrated typed operations. Existing configuration paths are not all globally converted merely by importing the approval library; consult the acceptance register for remaining critical-change routing.

Historical v1.14 integration scope: the installed response-service boundary is separate from the ordinary-user desktop and sensor graph. Its native pipe authenticates the actual Windows peer token and verifies the installed service before requests. Source Python, a caller-supplied name or a same-user bearer secret does not become privileged authority. Immutable publisher/package pins, protected state and a restricted SCM identity require independent provisioning. The initial/default v1 profile remains diagnostic-only. Current 1.15 adds a separately enrolled, pinned v2 managed driver-policy executor; its unsigned policy and deployment limits are described in the current hardening chapter. Native PID-bound process-egress enforcement remains unavailable. A path firewall rule or observed connection cannot prove PID-birth-bound socket admission.

Settings \> General and Full Setup expose separate opt-ins for local Windows session events and current-user Chromium extension manifest inventory. Identity Session Guard performs collection on its worker. Windows event access denial, log clearing, retention loss and cursor rollback remain coverage gaps. Manifests supply unverified extension IDs, versions and declared permissions; they do not prove an extension is enabled or has those permissions granted. Neither collector reads credential values, cookies, browser history or page contents. An external identity-provider connector requires a separately authenticated configured source; none is invented or enabled by default.

Open Adaptation \> Independent Recovery while Immutable Recovery Assurance Guard is running and the workspace has no UGCAP hold. Enroll the separately trusted recovery authority's 32-byte Ed25519 PUBLIC key in base64 form. Explicitly select the authorized local encrypted archive and its signed copy statement. Supply its original 32-byte encryption key and 32-byte proof/audit key, or leave both fields empty to request this user's existing protected recovery-drill keys. The workflow does not generate substitute keys. One-shot inputs are copied to bounded worker requests and wiped best effort; Python/Qt temporary copies cannot be fully erased.

A drill extracts the selected authenticated file inventory into a new private directory and rereads its bytes; it never overwrites the live workspace. The latest tested archive's signed revision, checked age and measured restore duration are shown separately from latest signed-copy evidence. A revision is the enrolled signer's association with that archive. The proof does not reconstruct or verify a full Git checkout or system revision. At most 16 plaintext private test directories are retained; capacity requires operator review and no automatic deletion occurs. Physical independence and survival of host loss remain separately verified deployment properties.

Recurring recovery tests require explicit consent, a previously verified selected archive and reusable original keys already in protected storage. Choose an interval from 1 through 720 hours. The existing recovery worker owns scheduling; a UGCAP hold pauses admission, and worker/process stop disables recurrence and clears queued one-shot material. Closing the panel leaves admitted work with its guard owner. Native filesystem calls cannot be forcibly preempted, so a pending cancellation cannot be reported as completed.

Guided prevention extends the adaptation review toward logging, App Control, memory integrity, vulnerable-driver blocking and Secure Boot. Each control must distinguish requested configuration from effective runtime evidence, describe compatibility and recovery, and use an enrolled typed privileged backend for mutation. Firmware changes, unreviewed App Control policies and unavailable native enforcement stay held. A changed registry value or successful command is insufficient evidence that a reboot-dependent protection is running.

For replay quality, [tools/evaluate\_detections.py](../tools/evaluate_detections.py) accepts --training-cohort PATH in addition to the evaluation cohort and active/candidate packages. It rejects duplicate evaluation payloads and exact event overlap with declared training sets or rule fixtures, regardless of renamed record IDs, revisions or changed labels. It binds the resulting cohort and package digests while retaining false positives and missed detections. Synthetic replay does not prove independent label review, semantic disjointness, exclusion of undeclared training or live-host efficacy. Release signing remains behind its separately administered authority gate; the repository does not generate replacement signing identities.

The October 22 live loop also corrected two observation/closure issues. QApplication.quit can be cancelled by the dashboard's intentional close-to-tray handler, so the owned test deadline exits its Qt event loop directly and still runs normal application cleanup. Separately, the Black Box reverse animation can hide a window before final close; its standalone entry now exits only after an accepted close confirms that readers have retired. Preserve actual process exit evidence and distinguish a harness mistake from a detector failure.

### 1 November recorder admission and shutdown follow up

Recorder delivery: The EventBus recorder subscriber now signs when needed and uses bounded memory admission only. A publisher performs no disk I/O, capacity wait or sleep. Exhausted, stopping or unavailable lanes raise RecorderAdmissionRejected; EventBus counts that subscriber failure and continues its other callbacks. Already admitted queues and original stored/spooled events are preserved. No synthetic coverage event or response authority is created.

Status and shutdown: Runtime status and ingest-status show admission\_rejected, separate saturated/stopping/unavailable counts and the coverage\_gap latch. These are process-lifetime, nondurable counters; a new process cannot certify earlier continuity, and other subscribers may still have received a rejected recorder delivery. Worker availability remains separate from the gap. Stop/start generations stay fenced through all stop callers' finalization. Only the last caller can remove identity-matched wake tokens after workers retire; real queued events make the drain incomplete and remain restartable. Neither an empty queue nor thread retirement certifies an in-flight batch after an unexpected worker crash.

Validation and remaining storage work: The focused gate passed 144 tests with one unavailable-symlink skip in 57.86 seconds. A separate Full60/normal STOP run met bounded lifecycle acceptance: native exit zero, 48 observed generations retired, 52 signaled waits, and unchanged source/preferences. Offline saturation tests are separate from this ordinary live run. Published advisory/setup commit 7ebb387 passed 15 hosted jobs; the later recorder revision needs separate check receipts. Primary database row retention is not a byte quota; durable remediation journals share that database. Raw dashboard stdout/stderr and native/external writes remain outside normal message budgets, and direct-startup fallback scratch history lacks an aggregate limit. Byte/free-space enforcement remains design work, with no new startup gate or automatic evidence deletion. Native P0, unknown coverage and independent deployment requirements remain; no Optimus actor is established.

### 1 November recorder commit boundary follow up

Commit boundary: Single-event, batch and replay inserts now leave their retry/fallback scope after SQLite commit returns successfully. The single-event identifier and batch/replay maximum identifier are captured before commit. If that lookup fails, the uncommitted transaction is rolled back before retry or authenticated fallback. A postcommit maintenance error no longer re-inserts or spills known committed events, or reclassifies newly replayed rows as duplicates. Replay can retain the first successful insertion counts and retire its completed source segment.

Revision and maintenance: The memory-only dashboard revision is published before optional pruning as a monotonic committed-identifier high-water mark. It can name an event that retention subsequently removes. A revision-cache publication fault does not invalidate the known commit; the cache can lag until a later successful write. Retention failures roll back their separate pending transaction on this recorder connection, without undoing the earlier successful event/receipt commit. Write accounting advances once for that known commit. Existing HMACs, public result types and authenticated precommit fallback remain intact.

Validation and remaining exposure: The separate focused offline gate passed 64 tests in 26.89 seconds with zero skips, failures or errors, including 32 new fault-injection cases. Ordinary Full60 and normal STOP met bounded lifecycle acceptance: native core exit zero, all 45 observed process generations retired, all 49 retained waits signaled, and unchanged source and selected preferences. No storage fault or drive-full scenario was deliberately injected live. The injected failure paths use fixture-local keys and temporary SQLite/files; they do not establish the cause of the operator's earlier drive growth. No one-time retained history cleanup or rewrite was performed. This is not a byte/page quota, proof against commit-raised ambiguity or failed rollback, or a cross-process storage reserve. Shared writers, legacy entry sizes, physical storage growth and constructor failures remain separate. Native P0, same-user/kernel trust boundaries and independent deployment requirements remain open. Hosted acceptance for this revision needs separate exact-commit checks.

### 1 November optional audit admission follow up

Entry admission: Legacy RemediationLog.log alone admits a complete stored entry up to 65,536 logical bytes. It counts all UTF-8 SQL text fields, record JSON, actual receipt JSON and receipt hash, plus eight bytes each for id, timestamp, verified and host\_level. SQL text metadata requires plain strings; None/empty MITRE defaults and ordinary integer/legacy boolean verification values remain supported. Optional entries are rejected when known custom adapters for bound string, integer, float or NULL types are registered, without invoking or changing the registry. Unrelated adapters remain allowed. Typed invalid or oversized entries stop before INSERT; retained bytes, head, cadence, transactions, owners and recovery claims remain unchanged by that refusal. No one-time history cleanup occurs. Durable intent, terminal and reconciliation writers remain outside this optional limit.

Admission visibility: Copied counters use an independent memory lock, without SQL, path, clock or constructor work. They reset on instance replacement or restart and are not a durable loss journal. Pending calls remain distinct from rejected writes; the gap latch is not proof of complete history when false. Status JSON/TXT and remlog status expose the cached view, including empty-history cases. All seven optional caller branches aggregate per-call attempted, recorded, rejected, unavailable and persistence-unknown outcomes, shown separately from native results. Missing or malformed status remains unavailable. A complete syntactic writer acknowledgement is not independent authenticated proof. Closure gates, response authority and recovery rules stay separate.

Validation and remaining exposure: The separate focused gate passed 301 tests in 222.11 seconds, with no failures or errors and one skip because directory symlinks were unavailable. It included 95 new writer-admission cases and separate visibility regressions. Ordinary Full60 and normal STOP met bounded lifecycle acceptance: native core exit zero, all 55 observed process generations retired, all 59 retained waits signaled, and unchanged source and selected preferences. Oversized entries and custom adapters were not deliberately injected live. Generic database exceptions remain persistence-unknown, including a commit that may have succeeded before raising; known successful commits remain recorded through optional maintenance failure. Normal trusted SQLite binding is assumed. The adapter check is not a concurrent-registration fence or protection against a compromised process. Serializer peak memory, physical database/WAL quotas, shared writers, storage reserves, constructor failures and native P0 remain unresolved. Same-user/kernel boundaries and independent deployment requirements remain. Hosted acceptance needs separate exact-commit checks.

### 1 November telemetry storage and dialog recovery

Scope and defaults: The telemetry writer uses worker-observed database, WAL, SHM and volume facts with generation checks. Default admission targets are database 256 MiB, WAL 64 MiB and minimum free space 2048 MiB. Settings accept database 16–16384 MiB, WAL 4–1024 MiB and free space 512–65536 MiB. The fixed complete logical write unit is 1 MiB, including stored SQL text and escaped dead-letter representation. A bare recorder remains explicitly unconfigured for legacy callers; production GUI and headless startup install policy before asynchronous workers start. Constructor/schema writes are outside this policy, and it adds no startup gate.

Operator controls: Settings \> System provides cached status and expandable targets; Full Setup maps the same four policy fields. Block for this run, Allow within targets and Apply now / retry change the current policy in memory. Save separately persists the choice. Accepted Allow means worker facts are still required, not that writes resumed. Closing, Escape or Keep does not change policy. Nonmodal warnings are deduplicated and bounded; this surface adds no database-delete, automatic history cleanup, checkpoint or vacuum action.

Pending work and counters: A typed storage hold retains acknowledged committed/spooled prefixes and parks bounded per-lane pending work instead of retrying it as a generic write failure or spilling new held deliveries. Already admitted finite units may finish after a newer Block. STOP wakes workers and reports an incomplete drain if volatile pending work remains; process exit can lose that work. Only an explicitly confirmed exact parked oversized token, with matching policy/worker/pending generations and no in-flight work, can be discarded. Recorded history, replay originals and recovery copies remain preserved. Rejection, user-discard and write-failure counts and their gap latch are nondurable. Hold, replay-deferral and maintenance-deferral counts are cumulative attempts in this instance, not present backlog counts. Missing or malformed cached observations remain unavailable with unknown counts; zero gaps do not prove complete persistence.

Dialog recovery and validation: Reveal coordination restores pending masks when a current target is destroyed and retains its close and shutdown fences. The reproduced source path is a plausible explanation for an outline-only window, not attribution of the historical incident or a native P0 fix. The fixture-corrected focused gate passed 447 tests in 89.48 seconds with no failures, errors or skips. A later disclosure-label source edit separately passed 447 tests in 70.12 seconds with no failures, errors or skips. Whole-source Ruff and the finite startup preflight also passed; their receipts remain separately scoped. The final disclosure-label epoch's ordinary Full60 and normal STOP met bounded lifecycle acceptance: native Core exit zero, 51 unique observed process generations and all 55 retained wait rows signaled. The 503-file source snapshot and selected saved preferences were unchanged. Child exit codes and complete process history were not established; no drive-full or storage-hold fault was injected live.

Remaining limits: These are sampled telemetry-writer admission targets, not an OS filesystem quota, atomic aggregate or guaranteed response reserve. The remediation journal shares the database; constructor/schema work, other/native writers, upstream serialization allocations and namespace attacks remain outside this policy. Native P0, same-user/kernel trust boundaries and independent deployment requirements remain unresolved. A named post-STOP comparison found both selected fault logs byte-identical to their pre-STOP copies, with no append. It does not prove continuous logging, writer/hook health, finalizer coverage or the cause of a native fault. Earlier COM-labeled diagnostic growth remains unattributed. Historical hosted failures and new exact-commit acceptance are separate evidence.

### 1 November persistence baseline classification

Classification boundary: New Persistence Sweep baseline inventory carries observation disposition and finding kind, active\_attack=False and observe-only response authority, while retaining original HIGH/CRITICAL severity, evidence and unreviewed baseline state. Legacy recognition requires the normalized Persistence Sweep producer, HIGH/CRITICAL severity and an exact plain dictionary containing change, surface, entry, value, mitre, baseline\_trust and response\_authorized. The six text values must be plain strings; change is baseline\_enrollment, trust is unreviewed and response\_authorized is literal False. Extra or missing metadata refuses this projection. Existing explicit classification and active-signal branches retain precedence; real added/modified persistence changes are unchanged.
